moduleTitle: Lesson 8 - The Difference Between SOAP & REST
learningObjectives: Distinguish SOAP messaging from REST architectural constraints.
Scope HTTP method and authentication claims to the applicable binding and contract.
Inspect a service definition in API Scan.
Define expected outcomes independently of observed responses.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: SOAP and REST are different kinds of specification

elements.text: SOAP defines XML-based message construction and processing, with bindings to different underlying protocols. SOAP 1.2 HTTP binding associates POST with request-response and GET with SOAP-response; SOAP is not universally POST-only or HTTP-only.

REST is an architectural style with constraints including stateless interaction and a uniform interface. JSON alone does not make an API RESTful. Stateless interaction does not mean the server cannot store business resources. Authentication and session behavior must be determined from the service contract, not inferred from the word SOAP.

Independent guidance: avoid unsupported popularity rankings or a universal more-flexible/less-flexible verdict. Compare the required interaction, representations, security and tooling for the actual service.

Use an authorized sandbox and its current service definition. Scan the supplied file or URI, inspect operations, messages, namespaces and expected authentication, then send a permitted request. The historical DemoWebShop endpoint and account flow were not executed or certified here.

Independent guidance: distinguish a local display name from the operation QName, payload and endpoint. A rename is not a substitute for editing the service contract. Inspect technical fields and compare the returned response with explicit expectations; numerical prefixes do not schedule execution.

Inspect a service definition and identify the message binding, permitted operation and credential mechanism. Prepare positive and negative assertions. Academy video and exercise files were not accessed.

examPitfalls.title: Treating SOAP as POST-only
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Applying one familiar binding pattern universally.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the binding; SOAP 1.2 HTTP also defines a GET SOAP-response pattern.

examPitfalls.title: Equating display labels with protocol identity
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Using renamed labels as proof of the operation QName.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect endpoint, binding and payload fields separately.

examPitfalls.title: Inferring authentication from statelessness
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming SOAP requires username/password on every call.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented service authentication; statelessness does not erase server business data.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What defines the SOAP message structure?

options.text: An XML-based envelope and processing model.
Any JSON document is automatically SOAP.
Any arbitrary binary data without a message model.

practiceQuiz.rationale: SOAP uses an XML-based message model; the selected binding controls its transport.

optionExplanations.A: This states the message model without falsely restricting all transports.
optionExplanations.B: JSON alone is not a SOAP envelope.
optionExplanations.C: SOAP is not a JSON-only protocol.
optionExplanations.D: SOAP has defined construction and processing rules.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What should a tester use to establish a SOAP service operation and binding?

options.text: A remembered demo URL without checking it.
The current service definition and authorized sandbox contract.
Assume every service has the same operations.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Service-specific operations, bindings and authentication need evidence.

optionExplanations.A: A historical URL may be stale or unrelated.
optionExplanations.B: The current contract provides the relevant technical definition.
optionExplanations.C: A screenshot is not a binding definition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which action distinguishes a display label from protocol configuration?

options.text: Inspect the operation QName, payload and endpoint separately from its local label.
Assume a new label switches the HTTP method.
Assume renaming always deletes the endpoint.
Assume a prefix converts SOAP to REST.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Protocol settings require technical inspection; a label alone is not their specification.

optionExplanations.A: This checks the actual technical identity.
optionExplanations.B: A label is not an HTTP-method selector.
optionExplanations.C: Endpoint deletion is not implied by a label.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What determines whether credentials must be included in a SOAP request?

options.text: The service security contract and applicable authentication mechanism.
Every SOAP service uses the same access key.
Only DELETE operations can require credentials.

practiceQuiz.rationale: SOAP alone does not mandate repeated username/password credentials or prohibit sessions.

quickRecap.value: Request-response uses POST; SOAP-response uses GET.
Architectural constraints, not a synonym for JSON.
Inspect service definition, endpoint and security.
Display naming does not specify protocol identity.
Stateless interactions do not prohibit stored business resources.
